reason: The only substantive correctness concerns were in-scope claims c1 and c2: catastrophic FP32 cancellation in the real (a*c+b*d) and imag (b*c-a*d) numerator sums under the contract's per-component tolerance 1e-7+5e-7|target| over the complete finite FP16 domain. Both were rebutted by decisive runtime evidence: ~99k-row adversarial probes each (full-bit-pattern FP16 random search with directed cancellation selection to <2^-15 ratios, exact-zero-numerator rows with large products, extreme-value crosses including ±65504) found zero tolerance violations; max per-component error ratio was 0.177 for both real and imag, matching the theoretical bound (FP16×FP16 products are exact in FP32, and the sum's rounding error is ≤ half-ulp of the sum, keeping relative error ~2^-23 < 5e-7). The observed worst rows (num=[-65504,-65504], den=[1,16376]) confirm errors stay well within tolerance even at extremes. Problem.txt is the operative contract (no test.py/get_inputs), and the domain statement "EVERY combination of finite FP16 component values is legal" makes these adversarial cases in-scope — they were tested and passed. Skeptic reviewed the latest evidence and recorded no new claims; no open claims remain. Remaining low-risk notes (storage-offset views, subnormal scale, signed zeros) are contract-benign: signed zeros compare equal by contract, and the probes covered the full finite FP16 bit-pattern space including subnormals and extrema.
